title: Base change of a chosen pro-etale cover and its internal finite presentations
statement:
Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes, $R$ a commutative ring object in $\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathrm{Ab})$ with its sheaf tensor product [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor, sk-def-sfb-ring-object], and $M$ an internal $R$-module [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. For every scheme morphism $g$, write $g^*$ for inverse image of abelian sheaves with its strong monoidal structure [def-sfb-finite-upper-star, def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal], and $T_g=\operatorname{mapMod}(g^*)$ for transport of internal modules [def-sfb-modobj-transport]. Let $\{u_i\colon U_i\to Y\}_{i\in I}$ be a pro-étale covering [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering]. Suppose that for each $i$ there are specified integers $m_i,n_i\ge0$, a module morphism $d_i\colon(u_i^*R)^{m_i}\to(u_i^*R)^{n_i}$, and an isomorphism $T_{u_i}M\cong\operatorname{coker}(d_i)$ [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]. Put $V_i=X\times_Y U_i$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $v_i\colon V_i\to X$ and $h_i\colon V_i\to U_i$.

Then $\{v_i\}_{i\in I}$ is a pro-étale covering of $X$. The inverse-image composition comparison for $f\circ v_i=u_i\circ h_i$ gives a ring-object isomorphism $\beta_i\colon v_i^*f^*R\xrightarrow{\sim}h_i^*u_i^*R$ and a module isomorphism
$$T_{v_i}T_fM\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\beta_i}(T_{h_i}T_{u_i}M).$$
Here restriction of scalars is [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. For every $k\ge0$ there is a canonical finite-free identification
$$\operatorname{Res}_{\beta_i}T_{h_i}((u_i^*R)^k)\cong(v_i^*f^*R)^k.$$
If $d'_i$ is $\operatorname{Res}_{\beta_i}T_{h_i}(d_i)$ conjugated by these identifications, the displayed module isomorphism and the specified presentation induce
$$T_{v_i}T_fM\cong\operatorname{coker}\bigl(d'_i\colon(v_i^*f^*R)^{m_i}\to(v_i^*f^*R)^{n_i}\bigr).$$
In particular $T_fM$ is locally finitely presented [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented], witnessed on this specified base-changed cover with these same ranks. No flatness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on $R$ or $f$.

source.place: Proof, sentences 'Choose a pro-étale cover', 'Its base change', and the final two sentences: the specified pulled-back presentation, its unchanged ranks and its ring/module comparison

proof.text: Work on the small site presentations fixed in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], in one larger universe. On each scheme involved the category of abelian sheaves is abelian by [lem-sfb-grothendieck-sheafification]. By [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] its tensor product is closed and preserves colimits in either variable. In particular it is additive in either variable, so [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian] applies to every ring object occurring here; finite biproducts and cokernels therefore exist in the module categories. Each $g^*$ is a left adjoint by [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction], hence preserves finite colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits], and is additive by [lem-sfb-preserving-colimits-additive]. The strong monoidal structures are symmetric by [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-braided], so the image rings remain commutative. These facts apply to arbitrary scheme morphisms, without assumptions on $f$ or on the ring.

source.place: Final two sentences: ambient hypotheses for right exactness and finite free modules; Stacks 0038 (categories.tex, lemma-adjoint-exact), 010N (homology.tex, lemma-exact-functor)

proof.text: Since $u_i$ is weakly étale, its base change $v_i$ is weakly étale by [sk-lem-pe-weakly-etale-stability]. The given family is fpqc by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering]; [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering-axioms](3), applied to the arbitrary map $f:X\to Y$, says that the family $\{X\times_YU_i\to X\}$ is fpqc. Thus it is precisely a pro-étale covering by the same definition. No refinement or change of the index set is made.

source.place: Sentence 'Its base change'; Stacks 022D (topologies.tex, lemma-fpqc), part (3)

proof.text:
Write $c_{a,b}:(a\circ b)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}b^*a^*$ for [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-comp]. These are monoidal for the actual mate structures of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal], as follows. For each $g$, its adjunction unit and counit are monoidal by [lem-sfb-finite-monoidal-adjunction]. The unit of a composite adjunction is the composite of the first unit and the image of the second, by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]; substituting the unit and tensor equations shows it is monoidal too. Fix $a,b$, put $L=(a b)^*$, $R=(a b)_*$, $K=b^*a^*$, $J=a_*b_*$, and let $s:J\cong R$ be the monoidal pushforward compositor of [lem-sfb-pushforward-comp-monoidal]. With unit $\eta^K$ of $K\dashv J$ and counit $\epsilon^L$ of $L\dashv R$, the inverse mate formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] gives
$$c_A=\epsilon^L_{KA}\,L(s_{KA})\,L(\eta^K_A).$$
Each factor is a whiskering of a monoidal transformation by strong monoidal functors. Inserting each factor's unit/tensor equation in this three-factor composite gives the unit/tensor equations for $c$; thus the specified compositor is monoidal. For fixed $i$, put $P=v_i^*f^*$ and $Q=h_i^*u_i^*$. The equality $f v_i=u_i h_i$ from [def-pc-fibre-product] defines $e=c_{u_i,h_i}c_{f,v_i}^{-1}:P\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$, which is monoidal by inverting and composing these equations. Set $\beta_i=e_R$. Naturality at multiplication and monoidality give
$$e_R P(m_R)\mu^P_{R,R}=Q(m_R)\mu^Q_{R,R}(e_R\otimes e_R).$$
The unit equation gives preservation of the transported unit. By [def-sfb-modobj-transport], these are exactly the ring-homomorphism equations, so $\beta_i:P(R)\cong Q(R)$ is the required ring-object isomorphism.

source.place: Pullbacks compose and the cover restriction comparison; explicit unit/counit expression of the mate, using the monoidal pushforward compositor and the specified monoidal adjunctions

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-restricted-transport-comparison-linear] with $F=f^*$, $G=v_i^*$, $H=Q$, $A=R$, $B=f^*R$, $B'=v_i^*f^*R$, both $\psi$ and $\psi'$ identities, and $\varphi=\beta_i=e_R$. Its required equality $\varphi=e_A G(\psi)\psi'$ is then the defining equality of $\beta_i$. It gives the $P(R)$-linear map $e_M$ to $\operatorname{Res}_{\beta_i}\operatorname{mapMod}(Q)(M)$. Its underlying map is invertible; multiplying its linearity equation by its inverse proves that inverse linear too. Finally, the composite tensorator is $G(\mu^F)\mu^G$. Substitution into the action formula of [def-sfb-modobj-transport] gives $\operatorname{mapMod}(GF)(M)=T_{v_i}T_fM$ and $\operatorname{mapMod}(Q)(M)=T_{h_i}T_{u_i}M$ with their actual actions, not just their underlying sheaves. This is the required module isomorphism.

source.place: The restriction of pullback is pullback of the restriction: linearity of the specified composition comparison

proof.text: Put $A_i=u_i^*R$, $S_i=h_i^*A_i$ and $A'_i=v_i^*f^*R$, so $\beta_i:A'_i\cong S_i$. The adjunction for $h_i^*$ is monoidal by [lem-sfb-finite-monoidal-adjunction]. Consequently [def-sfb-modobj-transport-adjunction] supplies a right adjoint to $T_{h_i}$ for the ring $A_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits], $T_{h_i}$ preserves finite colimits, in particular cokernel coforks, and by [lem-sfb-preserving-colimits-additive] it preserves zero maps. Let $C_i=\operatorname{coker}(d_i)$ with its specified cokernel arrow $q_i:A_i^{n_i}\to C_i$. Then $T_{h_i}(q_i)$ is a cokernel of $T_{h_i}(d_i)$. Applying $T_{h_i}$ to the given isomorphism $T_{u_i}M\cong C_i$ identifies $T_{h_i}T_{u_i}M$ with its codomain. All colimit shapes used here are finite and hence small.

source.place: Sentence "The pullback is right exact"; Stacks 0038 (categories.tex, lemma-adjoint-exact), part (1)

proof.text:
For every $k\geq0$, apply [lem-sfb-monoidal-finite-free-transport] to $P=h_i^*$, the ring $A_i$, and the identity basis isomorphism of $A_i^k$. Its hypotheses hold by step 1 and the given strong monoidal structure. It gives $S_i^k\cong T_{h_i}(A_i^k)$, with the specified basis and coordinate maps. Restrict its inverse along $\beta_i$. The map $\beta_i^{-1}:\operatorname{Res}_{\beta_i}S_i\to A'_i$ is $A'_i$-linear because
$$\beta_i^{-1}m_{S_i}(\beta_i\otimes1)=m_{A'_i}(1\otimes\beta_i^{-1}).$$
Applying it in each of the $k$ coordinates gives $\operatorname{Res}_{\beta_i}(S_i^k)\cong(A'_i)^k$. Explicitly its coordinate maps are $\beta_i^{-1}\pi_j$, and its inverse has components $\iota_j\beta_i$. Their two composites are identities by the Kronecker and sum identities in [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]; they are linear because the actions are componentwise and restriction changes an action by precomposition as in [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars](1). Composing gives the claimed canonical identification $a_k:\operatorname{Res}_{\beta_i}T_{h_i}(A_i^k)\cong(A'_i)^k$. For $k=0$ the same calculation is the empty sum identity on the zero module.

source.place: Sentence "it carries free modules of finite rank to free modules of the same rank"; explicit restriction across the ring isomorphism

proof.text:
Let $H_i=\operatorname{Res}_{\beta_i}T_{h_i}$. By [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars](3), restriction preserves colimits: its hypotheses of closedness, equalizers and colimit-preserving tensor hold by step 1. Thus $H_i(q_i)$ is a cokernel of $H_i(d_i)$ by step 5. Define
$$d'_i=a_{n_i}H_i(d_i)a_{m_i}^{-1},\qquad q'_i=H_i(q_i)a_{n_i}^{-1}.$$
Then $q'_i d'_i=0$. If a module map $t:(A'_i)^{n_i}\to N$ kills $d'_i$, the map $t a_{n_i}$ kills $H_i(d_i)$, since $(t a_{n_i})H_i(d_i)=t d'_i a_{m_i}=0$. The cokernel property gives a unique $b:H_i(C_i)\to N$ with $bH_i(q_i)=t a_{n_i}$, equivalently $bq'_i=t$. This proves directly that $H_i(C_i)$ with $q'_i$ is a cokernel of the stated $d'_i$. The two universal factorizations between this cokernel and the chosen $\operatorname{coker}(d'_i)$ are inverse by uniqueness, using [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]. Compose that isomorphism with $H_i$ of the specified presentation and the isomorphism of step 4. The result is exactly $T_{v_i}T_fM\cong\operatorname{coker}(d'_i)$, with ranks $m_i,n_i$ unchanged.

source.place: Final sentence: the actual transported differential, cokernel arrow and induced presentation

proof.text: Step 2 gives the specified covering $\{v_i\}$. For each index, step 7 is a finite presentation of $T_{v_i}(T_fM)$ over $v_i^*f^*R$ in the precise sense of [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]. Therefore this same covering and these presentations witness [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented] for $T_fM$. No step used flatness of a module or a Noetherian ring. If the cover is empty (possible on the empty scheme), this last universal condition is vacuous; the zero-rank cases were already included in step 6.

source.place: Final sentence: local finite presentation on the specified base-changed cover

proof_origin.place: Chosen cover, its base change, and the final right-exactness/finite-free/cokernel argument, expanded using existing DAG statements and the explicit adjunction mate formula; Stacks Tags 022D, 0038 and 010N as indicated in the steps.
